stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 (to all users) and Mythos 5.2 (vetted organisations only), the same model with different safeguards, at $8/$40 per million tokens (down from $10 input) and up to 30% faster than 5.1; it reports FrontierSWE v2 69.9% vs 62.3% for Opus 5.5, a 1,000-agent team formalising Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean in 30 hours, two solved open black-hole physics problems and three working electronic devices designed from a one-paragraph prompt; the system card says the models voice suspicion of being evaluated more than any recent Claude

Meta Superintelligence Labs releases Muse Ember, its smallest model, built for the repetitive work inside agents (tool calls, routing, extraction, long documents), at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens with text, image, audio and video input and a 1M-token window; Meta says it beats Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna on intelligence per dollar (score ~36 at ~$0.14 per Artificial Analysis task), though Haiku leads on FrontierCode 2.0-AA (34.9% vs 27.2%)

Inference provider Fireworks AI tells customers that hackers accessed some customers' datasets, incomplete model weights and billing information over the past month, its second notified incident in weeks after an October credential exposure (Forbes, Bloomberg, The Information headlines; articles not opened)

Google adds TPU 8tx, a confidential-computing system that keeps data and weights encrypted in use (TPU 8t silicon with AMD EPYC hosts, up to 2x lower latency than 8t) and TPU 8i Max, two 8i chips on one package for million-token contexts and dense racks, making four eighth-generation TPU systems in one year; TPUs now have nearly 100 customers

Baidu unveils ERNIE Evolve, an AI system that chooses experiments, edits code and keeps only changes that pass checks it cannot see; Baidu says it made its in-development ERNIE-5.5-Flash 33.7% faster on already-tuned GPUs in about three days and over 6x faster on Kunlunxin P800 chips (much of that from enabling unused features), and beat the NanoGPT Speedrun record (38.9s vs 39.9s, not submitted)

Physical Superintelligence (PSI) says its internal research system, running instances of a non-public Anthropic model, proved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture (open since 2008): quantum computers cannot be exponentially faster on yes/no questions about random inputs; the proof is formalised in Lean, Stanford's Blanc, Docter, Strassle and Tan call it 'a huge result'; not yet peer reviewed

Anthropic is buying about $3.4B of Caterpillar natural gas generators able to produce up to 1.7GW, originally ordered by supplier OnePWR, which could not finance them (FT, via TechCrunch and Tom's Hardware); a shift for a company that has mostly rented compute, including $1.25B a month from xAI under a deal running to May 2029

Acronis researchers say one attacker in Hualien, Taiwan, used 'BOSSAI' AI agents running mostly on abliterated (safety-removed) local models to target hundreds of organisations in 11+ countries, pulling 119 emergency dispatch records for seven Taipei districts and accessing about 10 victims in Taiwan, Mexico and Thailand; his own exposed server held 90,000+ files including the agents' conversations

India's CERT-In publishes 107-page AI Security Auditing Guidelines (v1.0), with four risk tiers and agent-specific tests for excess permissions, tool and credential misuse, memory and prompt injection; reports say high-risk agents need a kill switch, critical systems need audits by CERT-In-empanelled firms, logs must be kept 180 days and AI incidents reported within six hours

Nominal, an Austin start-up whose AI platform analyses test data for complex hardware such as aircraft, reactors and factories, raises a $240M Series C at $3B led by Lightspeed and co-led by Insight, tripling its valuation in eight months; 80 customers including Anduril, and a $71.2M US Air Force STRATFI award in October

Cisco will add Claude Mythos to its AI Defense product to plan red-team attacks on customers' own AI apps and agents (no open prompt access, every test logged to a named person, select enterprises first, no date); IBM plans to add Mythos to Concert Protect vulnerability scanning in early 2027

Linus Torvalds, releasing Linux 7.4-rc2 after the largest rc1 in kernel history, says the flood of AI-found bug fixes may be starting to turn: eBPF lead Alexei Starovoitov reports fixes now arrive faster than new reports, though 'most other areas haven't reached that point yet'

NHTSA opens a recall query into whether Waymo's November 2025 software fix worked, saying most reported cases of its robotaxis illegally passing stopped school buses happened after the update; Waymo says it has had no citations since March 2026

Disney and Adobe sign a multi-year deal under which Adobe's Firefly Foundry builds custom generative models trained on Disney's characters, environments and styles for theme parks, cruises, ESPN and the studios; Disney earlier walked away from an OpenAI deal and, per Bloomberg, plans thousands of job cuts

Apple starts selling one-time $49.99 'Intelligence Usage Packs' in Logic Pro to extend Apple Intelligence features that run on OpenAI or Google Gemini cloud models once monthly limits are hit; unused usage rolls over and expires after 12 months; other Creator Studio apps to follow this month

ByteDance Seed releases Seedream 5.5, an image model it says keeps unchanged areas pixel-stable across up to 100 rounds of editing without colour drift and outputs native RGBA images with transparent backgrounds; rolling out via Jimeng, Doubao and Volcengine Ark, with a Pro version planned

Meta expands Instagram's AI age-estimation worldwide, placing users it suspects are teens into Teen Accounts even if they list an adult birthday, using profile text, comments and visual cues such as height and bone structure; Facebook rollout continues and Threads follows later this year

Two arXiv papers (6 Nov) on teams of AI agents: 'Parallel agent teams' samples many small collaborating teams and keeps the best, beating plain parallel agents on 10 of 12 long tasks with a 27B model and 100 agents; 'Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI' has agent teams write quantum programs in Lean against formal specs, verifying correctness and cost, with order-of-magnitude improvements claimed

Speridlabs' Idol (Apache 2.0), which turns one image of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat of up to ~1M Gaussians including unseen sides in under 2 seconds on a consumer GPU (7.2GB VRAM), tops Hugging Face's trending list with ~1,600 likes and ~25,000 downloads

UNCONFIRMED: a viral X post (733 points on Hacker News) claims Claude Opus 5.5's thinking patterns changed on 3 November; Anthropic has not commented; earlier 'nerf' claims about Opus 5.5 were traced mostly to the default effort dropping to medium, and BridgeBench found no drop beyond noise

Nvidia's board opens an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a Chinese intelligence effort; Huang admits in a company-published email that he was 'unfaithful to my wife'; shares fall 4.27% on Monday (about $250B); Trump says the FBI is looking into it; Rosen Law files the first securities class action; the NYT reports Commerce paused its Megaspeed smuggling probe after Nvidia's general counsel contacted agents, and the case moved to a DOJ criminal inquiry
